payload.friendly_name: hn serve: governed local Git server
payload.purpose_context: Hubnot checks policy and evidence only on the client today, so any credential with push access can move main directly, and multi-agent use needs manual per-actor and per-proposal selection. hn serve is an optional server that maps SSH keys to Hubnot actors, enforces governed protected-branch updates, advances main only to tested commits, fans out trusted facts to clients, and serves Git LFS objects, while every existing workflow over an ordinary Git remote keeps working.
payload.purpose_tldr: Add an optional hn serve command that hosts repositories over SSH and refuses protected-branch updates that lack Hubnot governance evidence.

payload.question: How does a protected branch first come to exist in a newly hosted repository, and what happens when its current tip has no valid policy?

payload.final_answer: OQ-11: The administrator seeds a new hosted repository's initial history with an hn serve repo subcommand that imports an existing repository. Creating an absent protected branch by push is refused. If the current protected tip has no valid .hn/policy.json, every update to that branch is refused with a structured reason; recovery is an explicit administrator action outside the governed push path.

options: pre-receive and post-receive hooks run by a forced-command wrapper that holds a per-repository exclusive lock for the whole receive-pack session
proc-receive hook that applies ref updates itself
reference-transaction hook with per-ref checks
Other
payload.question: Where does hn serve enforce the push verdict, and how are protected updates serialized?

payload.final_answer: pre-receive and post-receive hooks run by a forced-command wrapper that holds a per-repository exclusive lock for the whole receive-pack session
payload.rationale: pre-receive sees quarantined objects and a non-zero exit rejects every ref and discards the pushed objects (FR-012), verified by spike with git 2.53. Hooks cannot hold a lock across the ref update, so the wrapper takes a flock before starting receive-pack and shares the descriptor with it. Every check and ref update for one hosted repository then runs one push at a time (FR-022, NFR-005). post-receive records branch owners and the push log only after refs move. proc-receive and reference-transaction were rejected because they require reimplementing ref updates or split non-atomic pushes into separate transactions.

options: Fixed layout under the server user home ($HOME/.hn-serve) with an absolute hn path in the forced command
Configurable --home flag repeated in every forced command
Other
payload.question: Where do hn serve state, hosted repositories and the forced command live, and how does the forced command find them?

payload.final_answer: Fixed layout under the server user home: $HOME/.hn-serve/state (0700) and $HOME/.hn-serve/repositories (0700); managed entries in $HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys; forced command is the absolute path of the installed hn executable followed by serve git --key FINGERPRINT
payload.rationale: The server runs as a dedicated Unix user (OQ-7), so that user's home is the natural namespace and the forced command stays exactly hn serve git --key FINGERPRINT (FR-004) with no extra flags. An absolute executable path removes dependence on the sshd session PATH. Tests set HOME to a temporary directory. A --home flag would add a second source of truth to every authorized_keys entry.

options: Server-maintained ref refs/hn/serve/v1 pointing at a blob containing hn-serve/1, visible to git ls-remote
Custom SSH command outside the Git protocol
Other
payload.question: How does an hn serve remote identify itself so clients can tell it from an ordinary Git remote (FR-017, FR-018)?

payload.final_answer: Server-maintained ref refs/hn/serve/v1 pointing at a blob containing hn-serve/1, created by hn serve repo create and refused for every push (reserved-ref)
payload.rationale: Works through any transport and through the forced command without a new SSH command. Spike with git 2.53 confirmed ls-remote advertises blob refs under protocol v0 and v2. Identification is a usability guard only: all-trusted selection still sends every ref through client quarantine and validation, so a forged marker on an ordinary remote grants nothing (C-006, NFR-006).

options: hn merge PROPOSAL --remote REMOTE [--branch BRANCH]: publish own actor chain, then a forced single-ref push of the head with push options hn-advance and hn-expected-tip, then sign proposal.merged with commit equal to head
Single atomic push carrying the actor chain and the branch update
Other
payload.question: What is the wire shape of an advancement request and how does the client record the merge fact (FR-014, FR-015)?

payload.final_answer: hn merge PROPOSAL --remote REMOTE [--branch BRANCH, default main]: verify the remote identifies as hn serve; push refs/hn/actors/SELF; read the remote tip T; if head equals or is an ancestor of T run the fast-forward repair path; otherwise push +HEAD_OID:refs/heads/BRANCH with --push-option=hn-advance=CANDIDATE and --push-option=hn-expected-tip=T; on acceptance confirm the tip, sign proposal.merged with commit=head and head=head, and publish the actor chain again
payload.rationale: Two pushes keep valid facts on the server even when advancement is refused (FR-014), which an all-or-nothing single push cannot. hn-expected-tip lets the server name protected-stale-tip when another advancement won the race (US3-6, NFR-005), because the forced refspec stops client-side git from pre-empting the server verdict. Without --remote, hn merge keeps its --no-ff path unchanged (FR-016). Existing merge-fact validation binds only subject, head, policy and evidence, so commit=head validates without a protocol change.

options: Call the existing quarantine validators from the pre-receive hook against the quarantined push, with one documented server exception for candidates whose code ref has not arrived
Write a separate server validator
Other
payload.question: How does the push check reuse replication validation without duplicating it?

payload.final_answer: The hook reuses validateQuarantinedActor (extended with a hosted-prefix range so only appended commits are re-walked), replicationEventDependency, validateActorChains, validateExactEventReferenceClosure, validateIssueRelationships, ProjectIdentityContinuity, loadMemoryStreamAt, measureQuarantinedSelectionUnderBudgets and enforceReplicationBudgets, and reads hosted events through the existing batched verified reader collectIssueEvents. One server exception: a candidate event whose code ref is neither hosted nor in the same push is accepted without the code-ref dependency; its code ref is checked against the signed head when it arrives (FR-010).
payload.rationale: Reuse satisfies FR-007 literally. The exception is required because hn sync publishes actor refs before proposal refs in separate pushes; without it, the actor push would need the proposal ref and the proposal ref would need the candidate, so neither could land. Range validation and the batched reader keep NFR-001 within 5 seconds at 1,000 events; per-commit git show of every hosted event would cost about 2,000 subprocesses.

options: Refactor evaluateProposal into a policy-parameterized core; destination evaluation applies destination thresholds and actor lists to the same signed facts, matching decisions by the base digest they were signed against
Require decisions to be re-signed against the destination policy
Other
payload.question: How is a proposal evaluated under the destination policy when its signed decisions carry the base policy digest?

payload.final_answer: Extract evaluateProposalUnderPolicy(proposal, events, policy, decisionDigest) from evaluateProposal; evaluateProposal keeps its exact behavior by passing the base policy and base digest. Destination evaluation passes the destination policy and the base digest: approvals count only destination trusted reviewers, CI counts only requests from destination maintainers with results from destination trusted runners for destination-required pipelines, and acceptances or rejections count only from destination maintainers.
payload.rationale: Maintainers sign decisions against the base policy digest, so filtering by the destination digest would discard every acceptance whenever the policy changed. Applying destination actor lists and thresholds to the same signed facts implements C-004 and the edge case that evidence from actors removed from the destination policy does not count. Re-signing would change the wire format and the existing governance flow.

options: Add repository-busy and advance-not-maintainer; refuse refs outside refs/heads, refs/tags and the governed refs/hn classes with reserved-ref
Keep the initial list only
Other
payload.question: Which reason codes beyond the OQ-2 initial list does the plan need, and how are unnamed ref namespaces handled?

payload.final_answer: Add repository-busy (lock wait budget, default 120 seconds, exceeded) and advance-not-maintainer (an advancement request whose pusher is not a maintainer in both base and destination policy, FR-014). Refs outside refs/heads/*, refs/tags/* and the governed refs/hn classes, such as refs/notes/*, are refused with reserved-ref. Precedence for one protected ref is fixed and documented in contracts/push-verdict.md.
payload.rationale: OQ-2 calls its list initial, and FR-013 requires documented codes, so additions are allowed when documented. A bounded lock wait prevents a stalled client from blocking a repository indefinitely without a misleading code. Fail-closed handling of unnamed namespaces follows HN-003 and NFR-003.

options: Keep selection version 1 and add allTrusted with omitempty; print all-trusted only when set; not-yet-advertised actor and proposal selectors are a non-failure status in all-trusted mode
Bump the selection file to version 2
Other
payload.question: How is the all-trusted selection stored and reported without changing existing selections (FR-018, FR-019)?

payload.final_answer: Selection files keep version 1 and gain allTrusted (omitempty), so existing files and their bytes are unchanged. hn replication show prints all-trusted: true only when set. The remote must advertise refs/hn/serve/v1 at select time and again at every sync. Under all-trusted, exact actor or proposal selectors that are not advertised report status not-advertised, which is not a failure; exact memory selectors keep their current semantics.
payload.rationale: omitempty keeps FR-019 byte-for-byte for existing selections and keeps existing show-output assertions valid (NFR-007). Older binaries fail closed on the unknown field, which is safe. Rechecking identification at sync time stops an all-trusted selection from silently becoming a full import from a remote that stopped being hn serve.

options: Import refs/heads/* and refs/tags/* only, require a valid policy at every protected tip, set HEAD to the default protected branch, document manual recovery
Mirror every ref including refs/hn/*
Other
payload.question: What does hn serve repo create import, what must hold at creation, and how does an administrator recover a protected branch with no valid policy (OQ-11)?

payload.final_answer: hn serve repo create NAME --from SOURCE fetches only refs/heads/* and refs/tags/* into a new bare repository, writes refs/hn/serve/v1, sets HEAD to refs/heads/main (or the first --protect value), and refuses creation when any protected branch is absent or lacks a valid .hn/policy.json at its tip. Imported branches have no owner. Hubnot facts arrive afterwards through governed pushes such as hn sync. Recovery of a protected tip with invalid policy is a documented administrator procedure: run git update-ref as the server user while holding the repository lock through hn serve repo lock-exec NAME -- COMMAND.
payload.rationale: Mirroring refs/hn/* would host facts that never passed FR-007 or FR-010, which breaks the FR-017 claim that every advertised fact was validated on arrival. A protected branch without valid policy can never move through the governed path, so creating one only produces a dead repository; refusing at creation is fail-closed and gives a clear message. lock-exec gives administrators the repository lock without adding a governed-path bypass.

options: git-lfs-transfer pure SSH protocol only, objects under the state directory per repository, staged uploads verified then renamed under a per-repository LFS lock
git-lfs-authenticate plus an HTTP server
Other
payload.question: Which LFS transfer path and storage layout does hn serve implement (FR-020, FR-021)?

payload.final_answer: Implement the git-lfs-transfer SSH protocol (version 1: batch, put-object, verify-object, get-object; every lock command answers unsupported) with the standard library. git-lfs-authenticate is refused as unsupported-command. Objects live at state/repos/NAME/lfs/objects/OID[0:2]/OID[2:4]/OID; uploads stream into state/repos/NAME/lfs/incoming, are checked for size and SHA-256, and are renamed into place only while holding the repository LFS lock, after a quota recheck. The quota counts verified stored bytes only.
payload.rationale: hn serve does not run an HTTP listener (C-002, HN-001), and git-lfs 3.x prefers git-lfs-transfer over SSH (3.7.1 is installed on the test host). Keeping LFS state outside the bare repository keeps git gc and the push check independent of LFS. Verify-then-rename under a lock ensures interrupted or mismatched uploads are never downloadable and never counted (FR-020, FR-021, the interrupted-upload edge case).

options: Generated shell shim used as GIT_SSH_COMMAND that looks up the generated authorized_keys entry for its key and runs that exact forced command with SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND, plus one real unprivileged sshd test skipped with a reason when unavailable
Call hn serve git directly from tests
Other
payload.question: How do acceptance tests reach the server through the forced command (C-009, OQ-9)?

payload.final_answer: Tests build the hn binary once per test (existing buildOperationalBinary pattern) and generate one POSIX sh shim per client key. The shim reads the server home's authorized_keys, finds the managed entry whose key matches its configured public key, extracts the command= value and runs it under env -i with HOME, PATH, SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND and, when set, GIT_PROTOCOL. git, git lfs and hn reach it through GIT_SSH_COMMAND. A shim configured with an unregistered key finds no entry and fails as sshd would. One test starts /usr/sbin/sshd as the test user on a loopback port with a temporary host key; it calls t.Skip with the reason when sshd or ssh-keygen is missing or cannot start.
payload.rationale: Running the exact command string from the generated entry tests FR-004 and FR-005 end to end without root or a system sshd. env -i reproduces the minimal sshd session environment and proves the wrapper does not rely on inherited variables. The real-sshd test covers restrict and forced-command semantics that a shim cannot prove.

options: Strict grammar for git-upload-pack, git-receive-pack, git upload-pack, git receive-pack and git-lfs-transfer with one single-segment repository name; clean allowlisted environment; HN_SERVE_* set only by the wrapper
Pass SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND to a shell
Other
payload.question: How does hn serve git parse SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND and build the environment for git and hooks (FR-005, NFR-003, NFR-004)?

payload.final_answer: Accepted grammar: COMMAND SP QUOTED-PATH [SP (upload|download)] where COMMAND is git-upload-pack, git-receive-pack, git upload-pack, git receive-pack or git-lfs-transfer (the operation argument only for git-lfs-transfer). QUOTED-PATH is an optionally single-quoted, optionally leading-slash, single segment matching [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99} with an optional .git suffix, never .. and never a symlink, and it must be registered in server state. Anything else is refused with unsupported-command or unhosted-repository before git starts. The wrapper runs git directly (no shell) with an environment built from scratch: PATH, HOME, LANG=C, GIT_PROTOCOL only when it matches version=[0-9], HN_SERVE_ACTOR, HN_SERVE_KEY, HN_SERVE_REPOSITORY. Configuration such as core.hooksPath and receive.advertisePushOptions is passed with -c flags. Every hn serve subcommand refuses to run as uid 0.
payload.rationale: A closed grammar with no shell removes metacharacter and argument-injection classes listed in the edge cases. Rebuilding the environment means a client-sent variable cannot forge the mapped actor that hooks read. Passing configuration with -c means a hosted repository's own config cannot disable the hooks.
